claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 accurately reflects § 1910.132(a) regarding general protective equipment requirements, specifying when equipment must be provided, used, and maintained across the enumerated hazards and routes of exposure.
Claim C0001 faithfully represents § 1910.132(b), imposing responsibility on the employer to assure adequacy, maintenance, and sanitation of employee-owned equipment.
Claim C0002 accurately captures § 1910.132(c) design requirements for safe design and construction of PPE.

Paragraph (g) explicitly limits paragraph (d) so that it applies only to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, and does not apply to §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137. By omitting this governing limitation from its scope and summary, C0003 is overbroad and would improperly apply workplace hazard assessments under § 1910.132(d) to excluded standards like respiratory protection.

Paragraph (g) limits paragraph (d) to specified standards. C0004 omits this governing scope limitation, making the requirement overbroad because it applies PPE selection to excluded hazards like respiratory hazards under § 1910.134.
C0005 omits the governing scope limitation from paragraph (g), which restricts paragraph (d) to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, and excludes §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137.
C0006 omits the governing limitation from paragraph (g) that restricts paragraph (d) requirements to the enumerated subpart I sections.
C0007 faithfully reflects the informative note regarding non-mandatory Appendix B containing example procedures for hazard assessments.
C0008 captures the written certification requirements of § 1910.132(d)(2), but fails to state the governing scope restriction from paragraph (g) limiting paragraph (d) to specific PPE standards.
C0009 accurately represents § 1910.132(e), prohibiting the use of defective or damaged personal protective equipment.

C0010 captures the employer duty to provide training from § 1910.132(f)(1), but omits the governing limitation in paragraph (g) that limits paragraph (f) applicability to §§ 1910.133, 1910.135, 1910.136, 1910.138, and 1910.140, excluding §§ 1910.134 and 1910.137.
C0011 captures the specific training subjects under § 1910.132(f)(1)(i)-(v), but fails to state the scope limitation from paragraph (g) restricting paragraph (f) to specified standards.
C0012 states the employee demonstration of understanding and ability under § 1910.132(f)(2), but omits the governing scope limitation from paragraph (g).
C0013 captures retraining obligations and circumstances under § 1910.132(f)(3), but fails to include the governing limitation of paragraph (g), which restricts paragraph (f) to specified standards.
C0014 accurately states the scope boundaries established in § 1910.132(g) governing paragraphs (d) and (f).
C0015 accurately states § 1910.132(h)(1) requiring the employer to provide protective equipment at no cost to employees, including its qualification excepting paragraphs (h)(2) through (h)(6).
C0016 accurately states the exemption in § 1910.132(h)(2) for non-specialty safety-toe protective footwear and non-specialty prescription safety eyewear when permitted to be worn off the job-site.
C0017 correctly represents the exemption in § 1910.132(h)(3) regarding metatarsal footwear reimbursement.
C0018 accurately captures the exemption in § 1910.132(h)(4)(i) regarding logging boots.
C0019 accurately captures the exemption in § 1910.132(h)(4)(ii) regarding everyday clothing.
C0020 correctly captures the exemption in § 1910.132(h)(4)(iii) regarding ordinary weather clothing and items.
C0021 correctly states § 1910.132(h)(5) requiring employer payment for replacement PPE except when the employee has lost or intentionally damaged it.
C0022 accurately represents the permission in § 1910.132(h)(6) allowing use of employee-owned equipment without employer reimbursement.
C0023 correctly states the prohibition in § 1910.132(h)(6) against requiring employees to provide or pay for PPE unless excepted by paragraphs (h)(2)-(h)(5).
C0024 accurately represents § 1910.132(h)(7) specifying effective and implementation dates.
C0025 accurately states the note to § 1910.132(h) resolving conflicts with payment provisions in other OSHA standards.
